main_body: Timber-framed two-storey house: a large hipped tile roof over a half-timbered plaster upper wall and a cobblestone ground floor with a plank door, windows and a hanging sign
top_band: Roof slope from row 0 to about row 43. Orange/amber tiles with a pale ridge highlight at rows 0-4, then mid orange and dark maroon tiles. A dark eave line sits at rows 40-44.
evidence: Down a middle column the large tiled roof surface (lighter ridge, scalloped tiles) reads as a top slope. It ends at a dark eave line that shades the wall below. The vertical front face follows, with timber framing, plaster, a stone course, inset windows with sills and flower boxes, and a framed door. The roof, hip slope and wall match the construction of the Beodeul house references. Both the roof surface and the front face are clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile highlights across about 5-6 tones. The plaster has speckle. The cobblestones are shaded one by one in several tones. The door has grain and the windows have glints, with flower boxes and a carved sign. Outlines are dark brown or maroon tones that lean toward the neighbouring material, not neutral black. It is as rich as the references or richer, with no large flat fills.
